summary: In Greek mythology, the Neikea (Ancient Greek: Νείκεα) are the personifications of quarrels and disputes. They are counted among the children of Eris (Strife), born without a father, and belong to the brood of harmful abstractions whose identity is exhausted by the meaning of their name. They appear in Hesiod's catalogue of Eris's offspring but are not notably personified anywhere else in Greek myth.
etymology: The name derives from the Ancient Greek common noun νεῖκος (neîkos), "quarrel," "strife," or "dispute"; the plural form Νείκεα (Neíkea) expresses the several manifestations of contention they embody.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: The Neikea are listed by Hesiod in the Theogony (226-232) among the offspring of Eris, the goddess of strife and discord, who was herself a daughter of Nyx (Night). According to this account Eris, like her mother before her, bears her children alone, with no father named.

Their siblings, the other children of Eris, include Ponos (Toil), Lethe (Forgetfulness), Limos (Famine), Algea (Pains), Hysminai (Combats), Machai (Battles), Phonoi (Murders), Androktasiai (Manslaughters), Pseudea (Lies), Logoi (Tales or Stories), Amphillogiai (Disputes), Dysnomia (Lawlessness), Ate (Ruin or Delusion), and Horkos (Oath).

sections.heading: Character
paragraphs: As personified abstractions, the Neikea embody interpersonal conflict and disagreement rather than the violent warfare represented by their warlike siblings such as the Hysminai and Machai. They are regarded as little more than allegorizations of contention, with virtually no narrative or attributes beyond the sense of their name.
They are not notably personified outside the catalogue of Eris's children, and no individual cult or distinct worship of the Neikea is recorded.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: As members of the brood of Eris, the Neikea belong to a group of personifications that embody the harmful and divisive aspects of human life. Alongside related abstractions of falsehood and lawlessness, such as Pseudea, Amphillogiai, and Dysnomia, they represent the discord that strife sows among people.

This cluster of personifications situates the Neikea within an ancient Greek genealogy of evils, in which abstract forces of conflict are gathered together as the attendant troubles that Strife brings into the world.
